use_case_summary: Primary: chat-enabled operations assistant (multi-turn) for port ops -> tight P95 latency (<=150ms token generation target for short responses). Secondary: embedding-based document search for manifests (high throughput hourly batches). Reranking for candidate routes during surge periods.
sla_requirements:
- P95 latency target for chat: <=150ms per token for warm paths.
- Throughput: sustained 12k tokens/sec during peak 2-hour windows, burst to 25k tokens/sec for 10min with graceful degradation.
- Uptime SLA: 99.9% monthly for dedicated pool; audit logs and retention >= 1 year.
poC_scope: 1) 2-week POC on Dedicated: 2x A100-equivalent nodes reserved (estimated 80 TFLOPS total) + traffic replay from Feb peak. 2) Validate batching config and prefix/KV cache re-use to hit P95 goal. 3) Measure cost per token at 50/70/90% utilization. Deliver report with tuned configs and recommended commit level.
cost_model_summary:
High-level assumptions used in our spreadsheet: commit tiers considered = 2x, 4x, 8x GPU-equivalent. Base monthly reserved cost (customer-provided pricing) used as baseline; added overheads: network egress, storage for KV cache, monitoring/console premium. Utilization scenarios: conservative 50%, expected 70%, aggressive 90%. Per-token unit economics computed as: (monthly_reserved_cost + ops_overhead) / (monthly_effective_tokens) where monthly_effective_tokens = GPU_tokens_per_sec * seconds_active_in_month * utilization.
Example calc (4x tier): reserved_cost=$150k/mo, ops_overhead=$18k/mo -> total=$168k. GPU tokens/sec baseline=6,000 -> monthly_tokens@70%=6k*2,592,000*0.7=10.886B tokens -> unit cost ≈ $168k / 10.886B ≈ $0.0000154/token. At 50% utilization cost ≈ $0.0000216/token. At 90% ≈ $0.0000120/token.
Notes: TTL for KV cache and request distribution (short vs long context) materially change tokens/sec. Embedding workloads create bursty IO patterns; cost amortization recommended across workloads with different weightings.
recommended_commit_levels: Shortlist: 1) 4x GPU-equivalent commit — best tradeoff for their current traffic + 2x headroom for bursts. 2) Commit + burst pool: official commit 4x + 2x burst capacity billed at higher per-hour rate. 3) 6-month commit discount recommended vs month-to-month to keep ARR predictable.
routing_and_fallback_policy_notes: Need explicit fallback mapping: primary model (quantized 70B) -> fallback to smaller 13B variant if latency climbs, with automatic degradations at 95% utilization. Consider cross-region fallback only for non-PHI messages. Cache priming on shift start to reduce cold-prefix latency.
negotiation_points_for_SLA:
- Define measurement method for P95 (service-side token generation time vs end-to-end user-visible).
- Penalty / service credit thresholds and bootstrapping period for first 90 days.
- Clear definition of 'burst capacity' and preemption rules.
- Data residency clauses and KMS key custody responsibilities.
- Escalation path and MTTR targets for infra incidents impacting SLOs.
technical_risks_and_mitigations: Risks: low utilization increases $/token dramatically; unprimed KV cache leads to high cold-latency; embedding-heavy hours may saturate IO vs compute. Mitigations: shared opportunistic batching across teams, scheduled cache priming, staged rollout with canary traffic split, reserve minimal slot for critical low-latency paths.
